# everpure_azure_storage_pool_status (Data Source)

Reads the status of an existing Storage Pool: capacity, bandwidth and IOPS usage, and the alerts the service raises for it.

The values can be used in any condition Terraform evaluates. In a [`check` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/checks), a failed assertion is reported as a warning during plan and apply, and the run continues. In a `precondition` or `postcondition`, a failed condition stops the run.

The `current` values of `bandwidth_usage` and `iops_usage` are the peak over the last 10 minutes. `alerts` holds the warnings and errors the service raises for the pool, for example when used capacity is high. Their text is meant for people and may change, so match on `level`, not on `message`.

If the storage pool is unreachable, the read fails with an error that carries the service's alert message. Inside a `check` block that error is reported as a warning.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    everpure = {
      source = "PureStorage-OpenConnect/everpure-azure"
    }
  }
}

provider "everpure" {
  subscription_id = var.subscription_id
}

variable "subscription_id" {
  type = string
}

# Looks up a Storage Pool.
data "everpure_azure_storage_pool" "example" {
  name                = "pool-prod-east"
  resource_group_name = "rg-storage-prod"
}

# A check block reports a failed assert as a warning during plan and apply; it never
# stops the run.
check "storage_pool_status" {
  data "everpure_azure_storage_pool_status" "example" {
    storage_pool_id = data.everpure_azure_storage_pool.example.id
  }

  assert {
    condition     = data.everpure_azure_storage_pool_status.example.used_capacity_percentage < 75
    error_message = "Storage pool is above 75% of its maximum capacity."
  }
}

# To block a run instead of warning, read the status outside a check block and use it in
# a precondition.
data "everpure_azure_storage_pool_status" "gate" {
  storage_pool_id = data.everpure_azure_storage_pool.example.id
}

resource "terraform_data" "require_pool_headroom" {
  lifecycle {
    precondition {
      condition     = data.everpure_azure_storage_pool_status.gate.used_capacity_percentage < 90
      error_message = "Storage pool is above 90% of its maximum capacity."
    }
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `storage_pool_id` (String) Full Azure Resource Manager ID of the Storage Pool. Must be in the provider's own `subscription_id`.

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `alerts` (Attributes List) Alerts the service currently raises for the pool, in the order the service returns them. Empty when there are none. Do not rely on the position of an alert; filter on `level` instead. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--alerts))
- `bandwidth_usage` (Attributes) Bandwidth usage, in bytes per second. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--bandwidth_usage))
- `data_reduction_ratio` (Number) Data reduction ratio. It is 1 for an empty pool and can be below 1. The service rounds it down.
- `estimated_max_capacity_in_bytes` (Number) Estimated maximum capacity of the pool, in bytes. The service derives it from the used space and `used_capacity_percentage` with single-precision arithmetic, so it is approximate.
- `iops_usage` (Attributes) IOPS usage, in operations per second. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--iops_usage))
- `space` (Attributes) Space usage, in bytes. Null when the service reports none. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--space))
- `used_capacity_percentage` (Number) Percentage of the pool's maximum capacity that is in use, from 0 to 100. The service also raises alerts when this is high; see `alerts`.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `read` (String) Defaults to 1 minute. A duration string: a number with a unit suffix s (seconds), m (minutes) or h (hours); segments can be combined, e.g. "30m" or "1h30m". Used when reading the pool's status.


<a id="nestedatt--alerts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `alerts`

Read-Only:

- `level` (String) Severity of the alert: `info`, `warning` or `error`.
- `message` (String) Human-readable description of the alert.


<a id="nestedatt--bandwidth_usage"></a>
### Nested Schema for `bandwidth_usage`

Read-Only:

- `current_in_bytes_per_second` (Number) Peak read plus write bandwidth over the last 10 minutes, in bytes per second.
- `max_in_bytes_per_second` (Number) Largest bandwidth the service offers, in bytes per second.
- `provisioned_in_bytes_per_second` (Number) Provisioned bandwidth of the pool, in bytes per second.


<a id="nestedatt--iops_usage"></a>
### Nested Schema for `iops_usage`

Read-Only:

- `current` (Number) Peak IOPS over the last 10 minutes.
- `max` (Number) Largest IOPS the service offers.
- `provisioned` (Number) Provisioned IOPS.


<a id="nestedatt--space"></a>
### Nested Schema for `space`

Read-Only:

- `shared_in_bytes` (Number) Space occupied by duplicated data, meaning data shared among different volumes and snapshots as a result of data deduplication, in bytes.
- `snapshots_in_bytes` (Number) Space occupied by data unique to one or more snapshots, in bytes.
- `total_used_in_bytes` (Number) Total space occupied by customer data, in bytes. This is the space being billed for.
- `unique_in_bytes` (Number) Unique space occupied by customer data, in bytes.
